newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sun Hung Kai to close Singapore broking office.
newsitem.headline: Sun Hung Kai to close Singapore broking office.

text.p: Hong Kong's Sun Hung Kai Securities Ltd is to close down its operations in Singapore, industry sources said on Monday.
The company, which has been in Singapore since 1980 dealing in Hong Kong, Malaysian and Singapore shares, was expected to close by end November, said a source close to the company.
The source said Sun Hung Kai decided not to renew its annually-renewable broking licence from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), the de facto central bank, when it came due in September.
He denied market rumours that MAS had refused to approve renewal of the licence.
"The company decided not to renew as the group is looking for a new direction under the new management," the source said.
Sun Hung Kai was recently taken over by Allied Properties H.K. Ltd.
Industry sources said about 10 people would lose their jobs when the Singapore office closes.
Last month, some 50 staff quit Sun Hung Kai Securities in Hong Kong.
